risks.attackDescription: Attacker injects malformed or malicious input data that causes the process to behave incorrectly
risks.causeDescription: Insufficient input validation — the process accepts data without verifying its integrity

proposedMitigations.text: Implement integrity controls and checksums
Use digital signatures for data integrity
Implement input validation and data sanitization

proposedVerifications.text: Integrity check validation testing
Code review for buffer overflow vulnerabilities

risks.threatDescription: Process input tampering — attacker modifies input data to alter process behavior

risks.attackDescription: Attacker uses debug interface or firmware extraction to read memory and recover cryptographic keys
risks.causeDescription: Authenticator storage is software-only — keys reside in flash or RAM without hardware protection

proposedMitigations.text: Store cryptographic keys and credentials in hardware-protected storage (TPM, Secure Element, HSM)
Apply side-channel countermeasures (power analysis protection, timing attack resistance)

proposedVerifications.text: Encryption strength verification (correct algorithms, key lengths)
Verify side-channel countermeasures are implemented (power analysis, timing)

risks.threatDescription: Cryptographic keys in software-only storage — extractable via memory dump or debug access

risks.attackDescription: Attacker sends high volume of requests consuming all available CPU, memory, or file handles
risks.causeDescription: No resource limits or rate limiting — process allocates unbounded resources in response to requests

proposedMitigations.text: Implement rate limiting and throttling
Implement quotas and resource limits
Use load balancing to distribute traffic

proposedVerifications.text: Stress testing and load testing (k6, JMeter)
DDoS simulation testing
Rate limiting effectiveness testing

risks.threatDescription: Process resource exhaustion — attacker exhausts process resources causing denial of service

proposedMitigations.text: Apply side-channel countermeasures (power analysis protection, timing attack resistance)

Implement proper ACLs and role-based access control
Store cryptographic keys and credentials in hardware-protected storage (TPM, Secure Element, HSM)

proposedVerifications.text: Verify side-channel countermeasures are implemented (power analysis, timing)

risks.attackDescription: Attacker fills the data store to capacity or corrupts its index causing all operations to fail

proposedMitigations.text: Implement rate limiting and throttling
Implement quotas and resource limits
Implement high availability design with redundancy

proposedVerifications.text: Stress testing and load testing (k6, JMeter)
Failover and recovery testing

risks.threatDescription: Data store unavailability — attacker makes the data store inaccessible

risks.attackDescription: Attacker splices in a tap device or signal injector and manipulates data in transit without triggering any alarm
risks.causeDescription: Data flow runs through a physically accessible cable without physical protection

proposedMitigations.text: Protect physical cable routing with cable duct, conduit, or armored cable to prevent tap and tampering
Secure cable access points with tamper-evident seals or locked enclosures to prevent undetected splicing
Implement integrity controls and checksums

proposedVerifications.text: Inspect and document physical cable routing protection (duct, conduit, armoring) — photo evidence required
Integrity check validation testing

threats.attackDescription: Attacker disrupts or delays the response channel from Alarm Processing Controller, causing Debugger to stall or fail
threats.causeDescription: No redundancy or timeout protection — Debugger depends on responses from Alarm Processing Controller to continue operation
threats.threatDescription: Response blocking: Attacker prevents Debugger from receiving responses from Alarm Processing Controller

threats.attackDescription: Attacker modifies the response from Alarm Processing Controller to include elevated roles or permissions, causing Debugger to grant unauthorized access
threats.causeDescription: Debugger trusts response data from Alarm Processing Controller without integrity verification, enabling privilege decisions based on forged responses
threats.threatDescription: Response manipulation for privilege escalation: Attacker manipulates response to gain elevated access in Debugger

threats.attackDescription: Attacker forges the identity of Debugger and sends malicious data to Alarm Processing Controller, which processes it as legitimate
threats.causeDescription: Missing sender authentication on incoming data flow — Alarm Processing Controller cannot verify the true origin of received data
threats.threatDescription: Sender spoofing: Attacker impersonates Debugger to deceive Alarm Processing Controller

threats.attackDescription: Attacker attaches a hardware probe to the embedded bus and injects or modifies data packets
threats.causeDescription: Embedded bus carries no integrity protection or authentication — data is transmitted in plaintext
threats.threatDescription: Data tampering on embedded bus DF-6 between Debugger and Alarm Processing Controller

threats.attackDescription: Debugger claims it never sent the command or data that Alarm Processing Controller received and acted upon
threats.causeDescription: No non-repudiation mechanism on the data flow — requests from Debugger are not signed or cryptographically bound to the sender
threats.threatDescription: Sender repudiation: Debugger denies sending the request or data

threats.attackDescription: Attacker attaches a logic analyzer to the embedded bus and captures all traffic
threats.causeDescription: Embedded bus communication is unencrypted and physically accessible — data can be passively captured
threats.threatDescription: Eavesdropping on embedded bus DF-6 between Debugger and Alarm Processing Controller

threats.attackDescription: Attacker sends a high volume of requests via the data flow, exhausting the processing capacity of Alarm Processing Controller
threats.causeDescription: No rate limiting or request throttling protecting Alarm Processing Controller from high-volume input via Debugger
threats.threatDescription: Request flooding: Attacker overwhelms Alarm Processing Controller with excessive incoming requests

threats.attackDescription: Attacker uses the DF-6 interface to halt the processor, reads security keys and modifies execution flow to bypass access controls
threats.causeDescription: JTAG or SWD interface provides full processor access — attacker can halt CPU and modify execution flow
threats.threatDescription: Privilege escalation via DF-6 debug interface on Alarm Processing Controller
